### Describe the bug

The binary wheels on PyPI for 3.3a1 appear to be incompatible with the recently released (Jul 18) 3.15b4, leading to segfaults in the interpreter, at least when using the manylinux x86_64 images (`quay.io/pypa/manylinux_2_28_x86_64:latest`, `Digest: sha256:a61875a2f84cab7df8de222ff12cabc08ff86eb4ad402ac90ba7bdaed9600cca`)

Setting `PIP_NO_BINARY=cython` solved the problem. This previously worked with 3.15b3.

This was seen across multiple different proprietary projects so there's no common code snippet I can provide. But I can attempt to answer questions.

Maybe yank those wheels for now?

comment_data.body:
Thanks. Yes it probably is too early to be releasing binary wheels for Python 3.15. I think it's only the release candidates where they promise any kind of compatibility.

So I agree we should remove them. I don't think I can do it myself

I can remove the Py3.15 wheels later today.
I was planning to prepare a new release since a couple of days already. Will see that I get it done soon.
I deleted the Py315 wheels. Installations should fall back to the non-binary Python wheel now.

title: [BUG] 3.3a1 binary wheels incompatible with 3.15b4, crashes interpreter
